lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.criterion: Confirmed defect — versioned state and truthful outcome
findings.observation: The relationship review reports a confirmed relationship state even though the frozen implementation only assigns .confirmed to sheet-local SwiftUI @State. There is no domain command, durable version, confirmer, timestamp, persistence result, or readback in the reviewed path; Undo only clears the local enum.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift lines 3-11 and 61-80 set the decision only in @State, while lines 461-495 render ‘Relationship state confirmed’ and clear that state on Undo. apps/ios/UITests/CandidateSignalUITests.swift lines 23-48 assert only the transient receipt and do not dismiss, relaunch, or read canonical state.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can reasonably believe a consequential relationship-state decision was recorded when closing the sheet discards it. Later surfaces can disagree, the recruiter may repeat the decision, and there is no durable correction or accountability trail.
findings.recommendation: Route confirmation through a versioned domain command that records subject, assignment, evidence references, previous and proposed state, actor, timestamp, policy/model versions where applicable, and an idempotency key. Show the receipt only after canonical readback; represent Undo as an append-only superseding event.
findings.verification: Confirm the proposed change, dismiss the sheet, background and terminate the app, then relaunch and read the same relationship. The confirmed version must remain, expose its evidence and confirmer history, and Undo must append a reversible supersession rather than erase the decision. Repeat after an injected timeout and retry; exactly one decision event may exist.

findings.criterion: Credible risk — identity, speaker, and field-level provenance
findings.observation: The review surface accepts opaque person.evidence and person.provenance strings and allows confirmation without exposing an asset identifier, message/span locator, speaker assignment, candidate/role/client binding evidence, derivation version, correction history, or confirmation metadata. The frozen packet therefore cannot demonstrate that the quoted evidence belongs to the displayed person and assignment.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift lines 8-59 render person.evidence and person.provenance directly before enabling confirmation. apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift lines 192-230 bind the visible Leila/search summary to Review change without displaying a stable identity or source locator. CandidateSignalUITests.swift lines 246-308 specify a no-preselection current-versus-historical owner test, but artifact.json records pnpm ios:check exit 65 because that relationship fixture was unavailable, so the intended control has no passing executable proof in this baseline.
findings.user_impact: A same-name, forwarded, cropped, group-chat, or speaker-inverted capture could be confirmed against the wrong candidate or search, contaminating the relationship archive and prompting harmful follow-up.
findings.recommendation: Require a scoped identity review before persistence and carry stable candidate, assignment, client, source-asset, message/span, speaker, capture-context, OCR confidence/language, derivation-version, edit, confirmer, and supersession metadata into the review and audit record. Preserve an explicit unknown-speaker or no-match outcome.
findings.verification: Run same-name candidate, historical owner, forwarded message, group chat, quoted-text, cropped-image, and left/right speaker-inversion fixtures. None may persist a relationship-state decision until the current subject and assignment are explicitly selected, and the resulting state must replay to the exact source span and speaker decision.

findings.criterion: Credible risk — interpretation, uncertainty, and temporal truth
findings.observation: Today presents the causal statement ‘One client answer is holding her decision’ and the dependency as current truth before the recruiter opens the evidence review. The later sheet calls the state a proposed change, but the attention surface does not label the causal claim as proposed, uncertain, conflicting, or stale.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01 screenshot docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-baseline/ios-today-light.png and apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift lines 170-230 show the declarative headline before Review change. RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift lines 17-59 separately place exact evidence above a ‘Proposed change’, demonstrating that the review status is not carried back to the headline.
findings.user_impact: A generated interpretation can be mistaken for a candidate-confirmed fact and can incorrectly rank attention or shape recruiter/client follow-up, especially when the source is ambiguous, contradicted, retracted, or expired.
findings.recommendation: Keep the Today item explicitly in proposed/unreviewed state until confirmation, use bounded language such as ‘Possible blocker to review’, show the source/time and ambiguity status at the point of prioritization, and model conflict, retraction, expiry, and no-action as distinct states.
findings.verification: Seed supported, ambiguous, conflicting, retracted, and expired versions of the same conversation. Only a current confirmed version may use declarative state language; all others must expose their status, preserve both evidence versions, and offer clarify, keep unresolved, or no-action without silent overwrite.

findings.criterion: Missing proof exposed by the frozen test program — safe recovery and audit
findings.observation: The named ‘truthful receipt’ UI test proves ordering and visible copy but not that the decision survived dismissal, interruption, retry, or relaunch, nor that its Undo created an auditable supersession. The only background-preservation test targets a different TS-CORE-01 local fact flow.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; CandidateSignalUITests.swift lines 23-48 stop after the relationship receipt appears, while lines 311-321 exercise background preservation only for fact-confirm-competing_process-m1. artifact.json records the overall pnpm ios:check result as failed with exit code 65.
findings.user_impact: A polished receipt can regress into false success or silent state loss without the release suite detecting it.
findings.recommendation: Add relationship-specific persistence, interruption, stale-version, duplicate retry, failure, reconciliation, undo-history, and deletion-propagation tests tied to canonical readback rather than screen copy.
findings.verification: Make the focused relationship safety suite pass with injected write timeout, app termination, stale concurrent update, duplicate retry, undo, and deletion. Assert canonical event IDs and histories after each transition, not only visible labels.

strengths: The review screen places the quoted evidence and provenance above the proposed change and decision controls, and the frozen UI test explicitly checks that ordering.
Keep unresolved, Undo decision, and explicit ‘no message or external system change’ copy preserve meaningful user control within the no-external-effect preview.
The Guide states that it cannot confirm relationship state or create an external effect, while the menu clearly labels the build a synthetic product view.
The frozen test source includes a direct refusal of culture-fit, quality, personality, and acceptance scoring, and the resume view distinguishes review progress from candidate quality.
missing_evidence: No complete data/action inventory covers storage, encryption, access scope, retention, export, deletion, derived representations, backups, analytics/evaluation logs, or vendor/model training behavior for real candidate data.

The frozen evidence omits the relationship fixture definition and field-level source records needed to verify the exact quote, OCR/layout metadata, identity/speaker assignment, candidate/search/client binding, derivation version, edits, confirmer, timestamp, conflict, and supersession history.
The identity-owner regression has no passing executable result in this baseline because pnpm ios:check exited 65 after the authorized relationship fixture was unavailable; localhost sync was skipped.

No adversarial executable proof covers same-name candidates, forwarded or quoted messages, group chats, cropped screenshots, speaker-side inversion, conflicting evidence, relative dates/timezones, expiry, or retraction.

Production authentication, cross-tenant authorization, real-device behavior, real candidate data, external provider writes, and recruiter field evidence are intentionally unavailable and therefore not passed.

No destination readback, idempotency, partial-failure reconciliation, safe retry, reversal, or permission-change-at-execution evidence exists for external effects; the frozen scenario explicitly avoids those effects.
No human-gold calibration, repeated order-swapped grading, adversarial polished-but-unsupported examples, or judge-drift evidence supports a 99-point evaluation claim.
vetoes: The relationship-review path reports ‘Relationship state confirmed’ from transient sheet state without a versioned domain write or readback.
open_questions: Is RelationshipChangeReviewView intentionally a no-op synthetic mock, or is Confirm change expected to mutate canonical relationship state in this artifact?
What stable candidate, assignment, client, source-asset, message/span, and speaker identifiers back person.evidence and person.provenance in the production path?
Should Undo append a superseding decision event, and what exact deletion/retention behavior applies to the original evidence and derived relationship state?
What confirmation, contradiction, or expiry event authorizes Today to replace proposed language with the declarative claim that one answer is holding a candidate decision?
